金剛般若波羅蜜經 <note>Diamond Prajnaparamita Sutra</note>

Form, sound, scent, taste, touch, and mental objects; this is what is called a <term>Srotapanna</term> <gloss>stream-winner, one who has entered the current of enlightenment</gloss>.
Subhuti, what do you think? Can a <term>Sakrdagamin</term> <gloss>once-returner, one who will be reborn only once more</gloss> think to themselves, "I have attained the fruit of a <term>Sakrdagamin</term>"?
Subhuti said, "No, World-Honored One. Why? Because a <term>Sakrdagamin</term> is named for coming back once, but in reality, there is no coming or going. Therefore, it is called a <term>Sakrdagamin</term>."
Subhuti, what do you think? Can an <term>Anagamin</term> <gloss>non-returner, one who will not be reborn in the realm of desire</gloss> think to themselves, "I have attained the fruit of an <term>Anagamin</term>"?
Subhuti said, "No, World-Honored One. Why? Because an <term>Anagamin</term> is named for not returning, but in reality, there is no non-returning. Therefore, it is called an <term>Anagamin</term>."

<summary>This passage explains that the various stages of enlightenment, such as stream-winner, once-returner, and non-returner, are names for spiritual progression that lack inherent, independent existence.</summary>
<keywords>Diamond Sutra, Srotapanna, Sakrdagamin, Anagamin, emptiness, enlightenment, non-attachment</keywords>
